source_locator.edition_or_translation: J. M. Ashmand translation from Proclus's Greek paraphrase; 1900 W. Foulsham & Co. new edition
source_locator.short_quote: Any two signs configurated with each other at an equal distance from the same, or from either equinoctial point, are termed commanding and obeying

calculation_dependencies: equal zodiacal distance from an equinoctial point

condition.relationship: equal distance from the same or either equinoctial point

normalized_rule: Classify two signs equally distant from the same or either equinoctial point as commanding and obeying.
synthesis_notes: This is a source-specific sign relationship, not a claim about social power or personality behavior.
review_notes: This rule records Chapter XVII's equal-distance criterion separately from the summer/winter semicircle lists. The source does not explicitly equate those lists with solar/lunar terminology.
transmission_notes: The equal-distance criterion is explicit in the Ashmand/Proclus main text. It is kept separate from the cross-chapter summer/winter sign-list identification and from later sign-familiarity systems.
